title: Southeast Asia's Race Season, Month by Month
seo_title: Southeast Asia Race Season Month by Month: 446 Races Counted
meta_description: When Southeast Asia races, counted from 446 road races: the busiest months, how Thailand, the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam differ, and what each part of the year holds.
dek: Southeast Asia does not have one race season. The Philippines fills August to October, Thailand runs from October to February, and Vietnam crowds into the last months of the year. Here is what a count of 446 races shows, and what it can't.

sections.heading: What the count covers
paragraphs: Run SEA's race calendar holds 446 road races across 11 countries: 122 in the Philippines, 100 in Malaysia, 89 in Thailand, 65 in Indonesia, 39 in Vietnam and 14 in Singapore, with a handful in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Brunei and Timor-Leste [1]. All but one have a race date, and those dates run from October 2025 to October 2027.

The count is not an even sample of the year. The calendar has tracked races in full since mid-2026, so 377 of the 445 dated races (85%) fall between August 2026 and January 2027. February to July is thin because most of those months' races had already been run when tracking began, and most 2027 editions have not been announced yet [1]. The month-by-month figures below are firm for August to December. For the first half of the year they show which races are already confirmed, not how busy those months will end up.

sections.heading: The busy stretch: August to December
paragraphs: Across the region, 339 races fell in the five months from August to December 2026: 60 in August, 50 in September, 78 in October, 83 in November and 68 in December [1]. October and November are the peak. The single busiest date was Sunday 6 December 2026, with 28 races on the calendar, followed by 25 October with 20.
The marathons follow the same shape but peak twice. Of the 146 races whose headline distance is the marathon, 29 are in August and 28 in November, with 20 each in October and December [1].

Racing here is a Sunday habit. 395 of the 445 dated races (89%) are on a Sunday and 48 on a Saturday [1]. On the busiest Sunday, 6 December 2026, races were set in nine countries, from seven in the Philippines and six in Indonesia to one each in Singapore, Brunei, Cambodia and Laos [1].

sections.heading: Every country has its own season
paragraphs: Thailand runs from October to February. 72 of its 89 races (81%) fall in those five months, with December the busiest (20 races), against three in August and four in September [1]. That matches the Thai Meteorological Department's cool season, which normally starts around mid-October and lasts until about mid-February, although the department declares the start each year from temperature, wind and rain rather than on a fixed date [3].

The Philippines runs from August to October. 78 of its 122 races (64%) are in those three months, roughly 25 a month, before the count drops to 16 in November, 14 in December and 8 in January [1]. That busy stretch sits inside the rainy season, which PAGASA, the national weather agency, puts at June to November [4]. The country's calendar is not built around dry weather.
Vietnam crowds into the end of the year. 33 of its 39 races (85%) are between October and January, with November the peak (13). There were none in September [1].

Malaysia is the most even. It has between 12 and 18 races in every month from August to January, and its spring is already filling: four races in April 2027 and three in May are confirmed [1]. Indonesia peaks in November, with 17 of its 64 races, and Singapore's calendar is small and concentrated in October.

sections.heading: January: the second peak
paragraphs: January is already the busiest month of 2027, with 38 races confirmed and more being added. It is Thailand's big month for marathons. On the second Sunday of January 2027 alone, the 37th Bangkok Marathon, the 22nd Khon Kaen International Marathon and the Khao Yai Marathon are all set for the same morning, along with the Cebu Marathon in the Philippines and the Bac Ninh Legacy Marathon in Vietnam [1].

The following Sunday brings the 40th Chombueng Marathon in Thailand, the HCMC Marathon in Ho Chi Minh City, the Kota Kinabalu Marathon in Sabah and the Iloilo Dinagyang Marathon [1]. The Buriram and Chiangrai marathons finish the month.

A January goal race gives the end of the year a structure. Training through November and December means planning around year-end holidays and travel, which disrupt routine more than most runners expect. Because so many January races share the same weekends, hotels in the host cities fill around the same dates every year, so book early.

sections.heading: February to July: fewer races, some fixed points
paragraphs: The first half of the year is quieter in the calendar, but it has its fixtures. Thailand keeps racing through February: 10 races are already set for February 2027, including Rayong Long Beach and the rescheduled Chaiyaphum Marathon [1]. March brings the Vientiane International Half Marathon in Laos and the Danang International Marathon in Vietnam. May has the Borneo International Marathon in Kota Kinabalu and the Terengganu Marathon.

June is a regular slot for some big names. Laguna Phuket Marathon has run on the second or third Sunday of June in every edition in our results archive, from 2019 to 2026 [2], and its 2027 edition is set for 13 June. The Jakarta International Marathon and the Phnom Penh International Half Marathon are on the same date [1].
Dates can move a long way between editions. The Manila Marathon was run in October 2024, August 2025 and June 2026 [2]. Check the current edition's date before planning a year around a race.

sections.heading: Planning a race year from this
paragraphs: For one goal marathon, the choice is mostly about where. Thailand's season makes November to February the obvious window there, Vietnam's big races sit between October and January, and the Philippines offers the most choice from August to October.

A runner based in one country can plan around its season: build through the quiet months and aim for one or two goal races in the peak. A runner travelling for races gets the most options in October, November and January, but also the most competition for flights and hotels on the busiest weekends.
The live calendar at runsea.run lists every upcoming race by country, distance and date, and fills in the first half of the year as organisers announce their editions.

faqs.question: When is the busiest race season in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Across the region, October and November are the busiest months in Run SEA's calendar of 446 races, with 78 and 83 races in 2026, and August to December as a whole held 339 races. January is a second peak, led by Thailand's marathons. The old idea of a June to September peak is not supported by the count.

faqs.question: When is marathon season in Thailand?
faqs.answer: October to February. 72 of the 89 Thai races in Run SEA's calendar fall in those five months, with December the busiest. It lines up with Thailand's cool season, which normally runs from around mid-October to mid-February, and January holds several big marathons, including Bangkok, Khon Kaen and Chombueng.

faqs.question: Are there races in the Philippines during the rainy season?
faqs.answer: Yes, most of them. 78 of the 122 Philippine races in Run SEA's calendar are in August, September and October, inside the June to November rainy season PAGASA describes. The count drops from November, and January has eight races so far.

Counts are by race date; 85% of dated races fall Aug 2026 to Jan 2027 because tracking began mid-2026, which the article states.
